proofs.proof_tex:
Put
\[
 \widetilde V_d=
 \begin{cases}
 Y_d,&S_d=1,\\
 \bot,&S_d=0,
 \end{cases}
 \qquad d\in\{0,1\}.
\]
This is a proof intermediate, not a new observed variable.  By
\texttt{ass:receipt-consistency}, \texttt{ass:selection-consistency},
\texttt{ass:outcome-consistency}, \texttt{ass:selection-exclusion}, and
\texttt{ass:outcome-exclusion}, a unit with response vector \(R\) produces
the state \((D_0,\widetilde V_{D_0})\) under \(Z=0\) and the state
\((D_1,\widetilde V_{D_1})\) under \(Z=1\).  Conditional randomization in
\texttt{ass:conditional-randomization} therefore implies, for each
\(x\in\mathcal X\), that the two margins of the distribution of this pair
are the arm masses \(q^0_{xdw}\) and \(q^1_{xdw}\) in
\texttt{def:observed-masses}.

We first prove the forward projection.  Fix \(x\).  Represent a response
type by an arc from its state under \(Z=0\) to its state under \(Z=1\), with
arc mass \(P(X=x,R=r)\).  If \(D_0=D_1=d\), the exclusion restrictions make
the two states equal, so this is a diagonal arc from \((d,w)\) to
\((d,w)\).  Denote its mass by \(d_{xdw}\).  Nonnegativity and the two
margin equations give
\[
 0\le d_{xdw}\le \min\{q^0_{xdw},q^1_{xdw}\}.
\]
The off-diagonal arcs from treatment zero to treatment one are precisely
the compliers.  Their left and right state margins are, respectively,
\[
 u_{xw}=q^0_{x0w}-d_{x0w},
 \qquad
 v_{xw}=q^1_{x1w}-d_{x1w}.
\]
The reverse arcs are precisely the defiers, with treatment-zero and
treatment-one state margins
\[
 r_{xw}=q^1_{x0w}-d_{x0w},
 \qquad
 s_{xw}=q^0_{x1w}-d_{x1w}.
\]
Consequently all four residual vectors are nonnegative.  Taking arc-table
totals yields
\[
 \sum_{w\in\mathcal V}u_{xw}
 =\sum_{w\in\mathcal V}v_{xw}=c_x,
 \qquad
 \sum_{w\in\mathcal V}r_{xw}
 =\sum_{w\in\mathcal V}s_{xw}=f_x.
\]
These are exactly the equations of \texttt{def:diagonal-residuals}.

Within the complier table, let \(h_x\) be the mass whose two endpoints are
selected.  Since the selected row and column masses are \(U_x\) and
\(V_x\), the masses of the four selection response types
\((S_0,S_1)=(1,1),(1,0),(0,1),(0,0)\) are
\[
 h_x,\qquad U_x-h_x,\qquad V_x-h_x,
 \qquad c_x-U_x-V_x+h_x.
\]
Their nonnegativity is equivalent to
\[
 \max\{0,U_x+V_x-c_x\}\le h_x\le\min\{U_x,V_x\}.
\]
By the already established \texttt{lem:ordinal-cuts}, the mass \(n_x\) of
selected--selected complier arcs whose right outcome exceeds their left
outcome satisfies, and is characterized by,
\[
 0\le n_x\le h_x,
 \qquad n_x\ge h_x-B_{xk}quad(-1\le k\le K-1),
 \qquad n_x\le G_{xk}quad(0\le k\le K).
\]
Moreover, by \texttt{def:selected-complier-margins},
\[
 a_x=U_x-h_x,qquad b_x=V_x-h_x,qquad
 \min\{a_x,b_x\}=\min\{U_x,V_x\}-h_x.
\]
Choose \(o_x=1\) if \(U_x\le V_x\), and choose \(o_x=0\) otherwise.  Then
\[
 o_xU_x+(1-o_x)V_x-h_x=\min\{a_x,b_x\}.
\]
Thus \texttt{ass:selection-minority-budget} becomes the branch budget in
\texttt{def:orientation-polytope}; \texttt{ass:defier-budget} gives
\(\sum_x f_x\le\delta_D\).  Every compatible full law therefore projects
into at least one \(Q_o(q,\delta_D,\delta_S)\).

For the reverse direction, take a complete reduced array in a fixed branch
\(Q_o(q,\delta_D,\delta_S)\).  For each \(x\),
\texttt{lem:ordinal-cuts} supplies a selected--selected complier coupling
of total mass \(h_x\) and strict-benefit mass \(n_x\), and supplies its
completion using the missing category \(\bot\) to a full coupling of the
margins \(u_x\) and \(v_x\).  This is the complier arc table.

The defier margins have the same total \(f_x\).  When \(f_x>0\), define a
table, indexed by the treatment-one state \(w_1\) seen under \(Z=0\) and
the treatment-zero state \(w_0\) seen under \(Z=1\), by
\[
 \rho_x(w_1,w_0)=\frac{s_{xw_1}r_{xw_0}}{f_x}.
\]
The division is valid because this case assumes \(f_x>0\), and direct
summation gives margins \(s_x\) and \(r_x\).  If \(f_x=0\), nonnegativity
and the margin equalities force \(r_x=s_x=0\), so take the zero table.
Adjoin the diagonal arcs of masses \(d_{xdw}\).

Every constructed arc determines a response type.  A complier or defier
arc specifies both endpoint pairs \((S_0,Y_0)\) and \((S_1,Y_1)\); when an
endpoint is \(\bot\), set the corresponding selection response to zero and
assign the unused potential outcome any fixed element of \(\mathcal Y\),
say zero.  A treatment-\(d\) diagonal arc specifies the treatment-\(d\)
response, and the response under treatment \(1-d\) may be filled in
arbitrarily because that treatment is never received by that response
type.  The arc masses are nonnegative, and their left and right margins are
exactly \(q^0\) and \(q^1\).  Since an observed mass array has
\(\sum_{d,w}q^z_{xdw}=p_x\) for both \(z\), these arc masses total \(p_x\)
in cell \(x\) and hence define a full response distribution.  Sample \(Z\)
independently of \(R\) conditional on \(X=x\), at the strictly interior
assignment probability required by \texttt{ass:assignment-overlap}.  This
establishes conditional randomization without changing either conditional
arm margin.  Receipt, selection, and outcome consistency and the two
exclusion restrictions hold by the construction of the response types.

The lifted law has defier mass \(\sum_x f_x\le\delta_D\).  Its actual
selection-minority mass satisfies, cell by cell,
\[
 \min\{a_x,b_x\}
 =\min\{U_x,V_x\}-h_x
 \le o_xU_x+(1-o_x)V_x-h_x.
\]
After summation, the branch inequality implies
\[
 \sum_x\min\{a_x,b_x\}
 \le \delta_S\sum_xc_x,
\]
so the law belongs to \(\mathcal M(\delta_D,\delta_S)\).  Its diagonal,
survivor, and benefit masses are exactly the prescribed \((d,h,n)\).
This proves the reverse lift and equality of the two \((d,h,n)\)
projections.

To distinguish the causal target from the reduced identifying functional,
define within this proof
\[
 \Theta_I^{\mathrm{causal}}(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)
 =\left\{
 \Pr_P(Y_1>Y_0\mid C,S_0=S_1=1):
 \begin{array}{l}
 P\in\mathcal M(\delta_D,\delta_S),\\
 P\text{ induces }q,\ H(P)>0
 \end{array}
 \right\}.
\]
For every lifted or projected law with \(H>0\), the definitions of \(N\)
and \(H\) give
\[
 \Pr_P(Y_1>Y_0\mid C,S_0=S_1=1)=\frac{N}{H}.
\]
The two projection directions just proved, rather than a definition of the
causal object, therefore establish
\[
 \Theta_I^{\mathrm{causal}}(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)
 =\Theta_I(q;\delta_D,\delta_S).
\]

It remains to verify the stated formulation size.  For each cell introduce
prefix variables
\[
 P^u_{x0}=P^v_{x0}=0,
 \qquad
 P^u_{x,k+1}=P^u_{xk}+u_{xk},
 \qquad
 P^v_{x,k+1}=P^v_{xk}+v_{xk}
 \quad(0\le k\le K-1).
\]
Then \(U_x=P^u_{xK}\), \(V_x=P^v_{xK}\), and the cuts in
\texttt{def:ordinal-threshold-cuts} have the constant-support expressions
\[
 B_{xk}=U_x-P^u_{x,k+1}+P^v_{x,k+1}
 \quad(-1\le k\le K-1),
\]
where \(P^u_{x0}=P^v_{x0}=0\) supplies the \(k=-1\) convention, and
\[
 G_{xk}=P^u_{xk}+V_x-P^v_{x,k+1}
 \quad(0\le k\le K-1),
 \qquad G_{xK}=U_x.
\]
There are \(O(K)\) original residual, survivor, benefit, and prefix
variables and \(O(K)\) constant-support rows per cell.  All other rows have
constant support per category, apart from the two global budget rows.
Hence the number of variables, constraints, and nonzero coefficients is
\(O(mK)\).  All coefficients are integers or entries of
\(q,\delta_D,\delta_S\); consequently the formulation has rational data
whenever these inputs are rational.

Fix an orientation \(o\) and abbreviate
\(Q_o(q,\delta_D,\delta_S)\) by \(Q_o\).  This set is a polytope by
\texttt{def:orientation-polytope}.  It is bounded: each diagonal coordinate
is bounded by an entry of \(q\); the residual equations then bound
\(u,v,r,s,c,f\); and
\[
 0\le n_x\le h_x\le\min\{U_x,V_x\}
\]
bounds \(h,n\).  It is closed because it is defined by finitely many weak
linear inequalities and equalities.  Thus every nonempty \(Q_o\) is
compact.

We first establish endpoint attainment without a positive lower bound on
\(H\).  A compact polytope is the convex hull of its finitely many vertices:
finiteness follows because a vertex is determined by a full-rank subset of
the finite constraint list, and the convex-hull assertion follows by
induction on the dimension of the minimal face containing a point, extending
a line through a nonvertex point to two boundary points of that face.  Write
therefore
\[
 z=\sum_{j=1}^J\alpha_jz^j,
 \qquad \alpha_j\ge0,
 \qquad \sum_{j=1}^J\alpha_j=1,
\]
where the \(z^j\) are vertices of \(Q_o\).  The branch restrictions imply
\(0\le N(z^j)\le H(z^j)\), so \(H(z^j)=0\) implies \(N(z^j)=0\).  If
\(H(z)>0\), linearity of \(N\) and \(H\) gives
\[
 \frac{N(z)}{H(z)}
 =\sum_{j:H(z^j)>0}
 \frac{\alpha_jH(z^j)}{H(z)}
 \frac{N(z^j)}{H(z^j)},
 \qquad
 \sum_{j:H(z^j)>0}\frac{\alpha_jH(z^j)}{H(z)}=1.
\]
Thus every branch ratio is a convex combination of ratios at
positive-denominator vertices.  If a branch has any point with \(H>0\), it
has such a vertex, and its minimum and maximum ratios are attained at such
vertices.  More explicitly, if two positive-denominator endpoint vertices
have ratios \(a\le b\) and denominators \(H_a,H_b>0\), then each
\(c\in(a,b)\) is obtained by placing weight
\[
 t=\frac{H_a(c-a)}{H_a(c-a)+H_b(b-c)}
\]
on the ratio-\(b\) vertex and weight \(1-t\) on the ratio-\(a\) vertex;
direct substitution gives ratio \(c\).  The endpoints themselves use
weights zero and one.  Together with the displayed convex-combination
bound, this shows that the branch image is exactly its attained closed
endpoint interval.  This
argument allows \(\inf\{H(z):z\in Q_o,H(z)>0\}=0\).

We next prove exactness of the normalized programs in
\texttt{def:normalized-endpoint-program}.  Write
\[
 Q_o=\{z:Az\le b,\ Ez=e,\ z\ge0\},
 \qquad H(z)=\eta z,
 \qquad N(z)=\nu z.
\]
For \(z\in Q_o\) with \(H(z)>0\), the change of variables
\[
 y=\frac{z}{H(z)},
 \qquad \lambda=\frac{1}{H(z)}
\]
is well defined and satisfies
\[
 Ay\le b\lambda,qquad Ey=e\lambda,qquad
 y\ge0,qquad \lambda\ge0,qquad \eta y=1,
\]
with objective \(\nu y=N(z)/H(z)\).

Conversely, let \((y,\lambda)\) satisfy the normalized constraints.  It is
impossible that \(\lambda=0\).  Indeed, the homogenized residual equations
from \texttt{def:diagonal-residuals} would give, for the treatment-zero
coordinates,
\[
 u_{xw}=-d_{x0w},\qquad r_{xw}=-d_{x0w},
\]
and for the treatment-one coordinates,
\[
 v_{xw}=-d_{x1w},\qquad s_{xw}=-d_{x1w}.
\]
Nonnegativity would force all these diagonal and residual coordinates to
zero.  Hence \(U_x=V_x=0\), and the homogenized inequality
\(0\le h_x\le\min\{U_x,V_x\}\) would force every \(h_x=0\).  This
contradicts \(\eta y=1\).  Therefore \(\lambda>0\), division is valid, and
\[
 z=\frac{y}{\lambda}\in Q_o,
 \qquad H(z)=\frac1\lambda>0,
 \qquad \nu y=\frac{N(z)}{H(z)}.
\]
The normalized feasible objective set is consequently exactly the branch
ratio set.  The positive-denominator endpoint vertices above map to
normalized feasible optima, so possible unboundedness of \(\lambda\) along
sequences with \(H\downarrow0\) does not impair objective attainment.  The
same equivalence shows that a normalized program is infeasible if and only
if its branch has no positive-\(H\) point; thus the endpoint programs also
certify absence of a defined target in that branch.

We now show that the finite union of branch intervals has no scalar gaps.
Let \(\mathcal D\) be the set of diagonal arrays satisfying the diagonal
bounds, the residual balance equations, nonnegativity, and
\(\sum_xf_x\le\delta_D\), before imposing the minority restriction.  These
are linear restrictions, so \(\mathcal D\) is convex.  The residual
quantities \(U_x(d)\), \(V_x(d)\), and \(c_x(d)\) are affine in \(d\).
Define
\[
 h_x^*(d)=\min\{U_x(d),V_x(d)\},
 \qquad H^*(d)=\sum_xh_x^*(d),
 \qquad B_x^*(d)=\min_{-1\le k\le K-1}B_{xk}(d).
\]
Because \(0\le U_x,V_x\le c_x\),
\[
 \max\{0,U_x+V_x-c_x\}\le h_x^*(d)
 \le\min\{U_x,V_x\},
\]
so \(h^*(d)\) is selection-feasible and has zero minority mass.  Each
minimum of two affine functions is concave; hence \(H^*\) is concave.  It
follows directly that
\[
 \mathcal D_+=\{d\in\mathcal D:H^*(d)>0\}
\]
is convex: for \(d^0,d^1\in\mathcal D_+\) and \(t\in[0,1]\), concavity
gives
\[
 H^*((1-t)d^0+td^1)
 \ge(1-t)H^*(d^0)+tH^*(d^1)>0.
\]

Take any reduced feasible point in the union of branches with \(H>0\).
If its recorded orientation does not select the smaller of \(U_x,V_x\) in
a cell, replace just that orientation coordinate by one that does.  This
does not change the continuous variables and weakly decreases the branch
budget left-hand side, so the same point remains in the union.  With
\(d,h\) fixed, define
\[
 \ell_x(d,h)=\max\{0,h_x-B_x^*(d)\}.
\]
By \texttt{lem:ordinal-cuts}, both the original \(n_x\) and
\(\ell_x(d,h)\) lie in the same closed cut interval.  Linear interpolation
of \(n_x\) to \(\ell_x(d,h)\) therefore remains feasible and leaves
\(H\) and both budgets unchanged.

Next put
\[
 h_x(t)=(1-t)h_x+t h_x^*(d),
 \qquad n_x(t)=\ell_x(d,h(t)),
 \qquad 0\le t\le1.
\]
Since \(h_x\le h_x^*(d)\), this path stays in the selection-feasible
interval and keeps \(H(t)\ge H(0)>0\).  The ordinal-cuts lemma makes
\(n_x(t)\) feasible for every \(t\).  Its actual minority mass is
\[
 \sum_x\{\min(U_x,V_x)-h_x(t)\},
\]
which is nonincreasing in \(t\), while the defier budget is unchanged.
Thus the path lies in the union and ends at the canonical point
\[
 \bigl(d,h^*(d),\ell(d,h^*(d))\bigr).
\]

For two canonical points, join their diagonals by
\(d(t)=(1-t)d^0+td^1\).  This segment lies in \(\mathcal D_+\).  Along it
use the canonical coordinates
\[
 h(t)=h^*(d(t)),
 \qquad n(t)=\ell(d(t),h^*(d(t))).
\]
Finite minima and maxima of affine functions are continuous, so this is a
continuous path.  It is feasible by the ordinal-cuts lemma, has zero
minority mass, obeys the defier budget, and has \(H>0\).  At each \(t\), an
orientation selecting a smaller margin witnesses membership in the union;
the orientation itself need not vary continuously because it is not a
projected continuous coordinate.  Hence the positive-denominator reduced
feasible set is path connected.  By \texttt{thm:projection-lifting}, its
ratio image is the causal identified set, and the map \(z\mapsto N(z)/H(z)\)
is continuous on this set.  To see directly that its image is an interval,
join points with ratios \(a<b\) by a path \(\gamma\), fix
\(c\in(a,b)\), and put \(\phi(t)=N(\gamma(t))/H(\gamma(t))\).  The set
\(A_c=\{t\in[0,1]:\phi(t)\le c\}\) is nonempty and closed.  Continuity
near \(t=1\), where \(\phi(1)=b>c\), gives \(\sup A_c<1\); continuity at
\(\sup A_c\) forces \(\phi(\sup A_c)=c\).  Thus every intermediate scalar
is attained.  There are finitely many orientations, and every branch endpoint
is attained as proved above, so the global minimum and maximum are attained.
Consequently
\[
 \Theta_I(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)
 =[L(q;\delta_D,\delta_S),U(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)].
\]

Finally we construct and verify the observable direction screen.  Write
\((a)_+=\max\{a,0\}\), and define
\[
 \underline f_x=
 \max\left\{
 \sum_{w\in\mathcal V}(q^1_{x0w}-q^0_{x0w})_+,
 \sum_{w\in\mathcal V}(q^0_{x1w}-q^1_{x1w})_+
 \right\},
\]
\[
 \overline f_x=
 \min\left\{
 \sum_{w\in\mathcal V}q^1_{x0w},
 \sum_{w\in\mathcal V}q^0_{x1w}
 \right\}.
\]
The diagonal bounds and residual equations give
\[
 r_{xw}\in
 [(q^1_{x0w}-q^0_{x0w})_+,q^1_{x0w}],
 \qquad
 s_{xw}\in
 [(q^0_{x1w}-q^1_{x1w})_+,q^0_{x1w}].
\]
The image of a coordinate box under summation is the interval between the
sums of its lower and upper endpoints.  Requiring the two totals to equal
the common \(f_x\) therefore gives exactly
\[
 f_x\in[\underline f_x,\overline f_x].
\]
There is no omitted complier-total condition in this calculation.  Indeed,
the observed normalization \(\sum_{d,w}q^z_{xdw}=p_x\) implies
\[
 \sum_w(q^0_{x0w}-q^1_{x0w})
 =\sum_w(q^1_{x1w}-q^0_{x1w}),
\]
so equality of the two defier totals makes the two complier totals equal as
well.

Nonemptiness of the target entails
\(\sum_x\underline f_x\le\delta_D\).  Every feasible point consequently
obeys
\[
 f_x\le \operatorname{cap}_x
 :=\min\left\{\overline f_x,
 \delta_D-\sum_{y\ne x}\underline f_y\right\}.
\]
Define the observable selected-state contrast
\[
 g_x=
 \sum_{i\in\mathcal Y}(q^0_{x0i}-q^1_{x0i})
 -\sum_{j\in\mathcal Y}(q^1_{x1j}-q^0_{x1j}).
\]
Substitution of the residual equations yields
\[
 U_x-V_x
 =g_x+\sum_{i\in\mathcal Y}r_{xi}
       -\sum_{j\in\mathcal Y}s_{xj}.
\]
Each displayed selected defier sum lies in \([0,f_x]\), and hence
\[
 |U_x-V_x-g_x|\le f_x\le\operatorname{cap}_x.
\]
Therefore \(g_x\ge\operatorname{cap}_x\) guarantees \(V_x\le U_x\) at
every feasible point and permits fixing \(o_x=0\); similarly,
\(g_x\le-\operatorname{cap}_x\) guarantees \(U_x\le V_x\) and permits
fixing \(o_x=1\).  If equality makes both rules applicable, either
orientation gives the same branch term.  A point in a discarded orientation
also belongs to the retained one, because replacing the chosen margin by
the uniformly smaller margin weakly decreases the minority-budget
left-hand side.  Thus the screen is observable and loses no feasible
projected point.

If \(r_{\rm amb}\) cells remain unscreened, at most
\(2^{r_{\rm amb}}\) orientations remain.  Solving the minimizing and
maximizing normalized program for each requires at most
\(2^{r_{\rm amb}+1}\) linear programs; infeasibility of either common
feasible region certifies that the branch has no positive-denominator
point.  The feasible objective sets are exactly the branch ratio sets, and
the preceding connectedness result shows that the smallest and largest
attained objectives are the exact pointwise endpoints \(L\) and \(U\).
By \texttt{thm:projection-lifting}, every branch has an \(O(mK)\) rational
extended formulation when \(q,\delta_D,\delta_S\) are rational.
Homogenization introduces only the scalar \(\lambda\) and multiplies
rational right-hand sides by it, so every normalized endpoint program also
has rational data.

Fix an observed mass array \(q\).  For a full law with \(H>0\), the causal parameter is \(\theta=N/H\), whereas \(\Theta_I(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)\) is the observed-law sharp identified set supplied by \(\mathrm{thm:projection\text{-}lifting}\), and \(L(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)\) is its lower-endpoint functional.  Thus these objects are distinct, and, on the target-existence domain, the condition \(L(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)\ge t\) is equivalent to the assertion that every compatible value of the causal parameter is at least \(t\).

Let
\[
 \boldsymbol\delta^-=(\delta_D^-,\delta_S^-),\qquad
 \boldsymbol\delta^+=(\delta_D^+,\delta_S^+)\in\mathcal B
\]
satisfy \(\delta_D^-\leq\delta_D^+\) and \(\delta_S^-\leq\delta_S^+\).  Fix an orientation \(o\in\mathcal O\) and a reduced array
\[
 z=(d,u,v,r,s,(c_x)_x,(f_x)_x,(h_x)_x,(n_x)_x)
 \in Q_o(q,\delta_D^-,\delta_S^-).
\]
By \(\mathrm{def:orientation\text{-}polytope}\), every constraint defining this branch other than the two budget inequalities is independent of \(\boldsymbol\delta^-\).  The defier coordinates and complier coordinates are nonnegative, so
\[
 \sum_{x\in\mathcal X} f_x
 \leq \delta_D^-
 \leq \delta_D^+,
 \qquad
 \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}c_x\geq0.
\]
The selection-minority row in the same definition and the ordering of the selection budgets give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_{x\in\mathcal X}
 \bigl\{o_xU_x+(1-o_x)V_x-h_x\bigr\}
 &\leq \delta_S^-\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}c_x \\
 &\leq \delta_S^+\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}c_x.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Consequently \(z\in Q_o(q,\delta_D^+,\delta_S^+)\).  Since \(o\) was arbitrary,
\[
 \bigcup_{o\in\mathcal O}Q_o(q,\delta_D^-,\delta_S^-)
 \subseteq
 \bigcup_{o\in\mathcal O}Q_o(q,\delta_D^+,\delta_S^+).
\]
Restricting both sides to \(H>0\) and applying \(\mathrm{def:identified\text{-}set}\) yields
\[
 \Theta_I(q;\delta_D^-,\delta_S^-)
 \subseteq
 \Theta_I(q;\delta_D^+,\delta_S^+).
\]

Now suppose that the target exists at \(\boldsymbol\delta^-\) and that \(\boldsymbol\delta^+\in\mathcal R_t\).  The latter assertion, by \(\mathrm{def:robust\text{-}region}\), implies both that the target exists at \(\boldsymbol\delta^+\) and that \(L(q;\delta_D^+,\delta_S^+)\geq t\).  The endpoint minima are attained by \(\mathrm{thm:attained\text{-}connected\text{-}endpoints}\).  Therefore the preceding set inclusion and \(\mathrm{def:endpoints}\) imply
\[
 L(q;\delta_D^-,\delta_S^-)
 =\min\Theta_I(q;\delta_D^-,\delta_S^-)
 \geq
 \min\Theta_I(q;\delta_D^+,\delta_S^+)
 =L(q;\delta_D^+,\delta_S^+)
 \geq t.
\]
Together with target existence at \(\boldsymbol\delta^-\), this proves \(\boldsymbol\delta^-\in\mathcal R_t\).  The target-existence premise at the smaller budget is necessary for this relative statement: enlarging budgets preserves a feasible positive-denominator law, but the reverse implication need not hold.

Assume next that \(q\) is rational and fix \(t\in[0,1]\).  By \(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}rational\text{-}charts}\), there is a finite semialgebraic stratification \(\{\mathcal S_j\}_{j=1}^J\) of \(\mathcal B\).  Each stratum is labeled model-infeasible, target-empty, or target-nonempty.  On every target-nonempty stratum there are polynomials \(A_j\) and \(B_j\), with rational coefficients and \(B_j\neq0\) throughout the stratum, such that
\[
 L(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)
 =\frac{A_j(\delta_D,\delta_S)}{B_j(\delta_D,\delta_S)}.
\]
Refine \(\mathcal S_j\), if necessary, by the two signs of \(B_j\).  This is still a finite semialgebraic stratification.  If \(\sigma_j\in\{-1,1\}\) is the resulting constant sign of \(B_j\), then on that stratum
\[
 L(q;\delta_D,\delta_S)\geq t
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \sigma_j\bigl(A_j(\delta_D,\delta_S)-tB_j(\delta_D,\delta_S)\bigr)\geq0.
\]
The model-infeasible and target-empty strata do not belong to \(\mathcal R_t\), by \(\mathrm{def:robust\text{-}region}\).  Hence the displayed sign tests on the target-nonempty strata give an exact finite semialgebraic description of \(\mathcal R_t\).

For completeness, the boundary conclusion follows directly from this finite description and does not require a generic-position premise.  Express each semialgebraic stratum by finitely many polynomial sign conditions, collect all polynomials occurring in those descriptions together with every \(B_j\), every \(A_j-tB_j\), and the four affine polynomials defining the facets of \(\mathcal B\), and take their common sign refinement.  On every relatively open cell on which none of the collected polynomials vanishes, all stratum labels and all robust-region sign tests are constant.  Such a cell is therefore contained either in the relative interior of \(\mathcal R_t\) or in the relative interior of its complement in \(\mathcal B\).  It follows that the relative boundary of \(\mathcal R_t\) is contained in the finite union of the collected algebraic zero sets.  Intersecting those zero sets with the finitely many sign cells and retaining exactly the pieces whose closures meet both \(\mathcal R_t\) and its complement recovers the boundary exactly.  This proves that the boundary is finite piecewise algebraic, including singular and lower-dimensional pieces; the included facet polynomials give the corresponding statement for the ambient boundary as well.

Finally, the original chart labels keep the three substantive boundaries distinct.  An interface between a model-infeasible stratum and a feasible stratum is certified as a falsification boundary.  Within the model-feasible region, an interface between a target-empty stratum and a target-nonempty stratum is certified as a positive-\(H\) target-existence boundary.  On a target-nonempty stratum, the conclusion equality is exactly
\[
 A_j-tB_j=0,
\]
because \(B_j\neq0\), and hence it is exactly the chart's \(L=t\) conclusion-boundary piece.  Chart interfaces are retained in the common refinement, so no boundary piece is lost when a formula or feasibility label changes.  If two or three kinds of boundary coincide on a lower-dimensional stratum, their separate feasibility, positive-denominator, and equality certificates remain attached to that same stratum rather than being conflated.  This establishes every assertion of the proposition.

proposed.statement: For every \(t\in[0,1]\), the robust region \(\mathcal R_t\) is relatively downward closed on its target-existence domain: whenever two budget pairs are coordinatewise ordered, the larger lies in \(\mathcal R_t\), and the target exists at the smaller, the smaller lies in \(\mathcal R_t\).  Whenever the fixed observed mass array is rational, the region has a finite piecewise-algebraic boundary obtained from the chart in \(\mathrm{thm:finite\text{-}rational\text{-}charts}\).  The chart separately labels the falsification boundary, the positive-\(H\) target-existence boundary, and the conclusion boundary \(L=t\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof of downward closure directly unfolds the orientation-specific budget rows and the identified-set and endpoint constructions, so these frozen nodes and the endpoint-attainment and projection results must be explicit dependencies rather than only transitive context.
